links.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT patient education responses versus recommended 6th-8th grade
links.effect: Mean readability scores 15±2.8 (preop), 16±3 (postop), 15.7±3.2 (intraop/technical); all responses above 11th grade, majority college-level; p=0.017.
links.quote: The mean readability scores for preoperative, postoperative, and intraoperative/technical questions were 15±2.8, 16±3, and 15.7±3.2, respectively, significantly exceeding the recommended sixth- to eighth-grade reading level for patient education (p=0.017).

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education responses
links.effect: All responses required above 11th grade reading level, with a majority at college-level comprehension.
links.quote: All responses required a reading level above 11th grade, with a majority indicating college-level comprehension.

links.outcome: Clinical appropriateness of ChatGPT responses to MISS FAQs rated by neurosurgeons
links.effect: Preoperative and postoperative questions generally appropriate; 50% of intraoperative/technical questions yielded inappropriate or unreliable responses, esp. radiation exposure and lasers.
links.quote: Although preoperative and postoperative questions generally elicited clinically appropriate responses, 50% of intraoperative/technical questions yielded either "inappropriate" or "unreliable" responses, particularly for inquiries about radiation exposure and the use of lasers in MISS.

links.outcome: Whether generative AI output is usable by patients with lower health literacy
links.effect: Responses exceeded the recommended reading level, suggesting utility confined to highly educated patients and potentially exacerbating disparities in comprehension.
links.quote: This limitation suggests that its utility may be confined to highly educated patients, potentially exacerbating existing disparities in patient comprehension.

screen.reason: The study evaluates ChatGPT's raw response accuracy and readability on frequently asked questions about minimally invasive spine surgery, evaluated by clinicians, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
